facts.text: The legislature makes the laws, the executive implements the laws and the Judiciary gives justice.
facts.quote: While the legislature makes the laws and executive implements the laws, Judiciary gives justice.

facts.text: Very sharp differences of opinion may lead to conflicts, which should be resolved impartially and according to the laws; for this an unbiased judicial machinery is required.
facts.quote: But if differences of opinion are very sharp they may lead to conflicts. They should be resolved impartially and in accordance with the laws. For this purpose an unbiased judicial machinery is required.

facts.text: Conflict of interests may arise between individuals and the government; people may approach the court for justice.
facts.quote: Conflict of interests may arise between individuals and the government. ... they may approach the court for justice.

facts.text: The court can help to bring the weaker sections of society, women, children, differently-abled and transgender into the mainstream of the society.
facts.quote: The court can help to bring the weaker sections of society, women, children, differently-abled and transgender into the mainstream of the society.

facts.text: When the common man benefits from freedom, equality and justice, it leads to the widening and deepening of democracy.
facts.quote: When the common man benefits from the values of freedom, equality, and justice, it leads to the widening and deepening of democracy.

facts.text: The Rule of Law is protected by the Judiciary; the law treats everyone equally and all are equal before law.
facts.quote: The Rule of Law is protected by the Judiciary. The law treats everyone equally. Rich, poor, developed - backward, men or women, all are equal before law

facts.text: The Judiciary helps to protect the rights of people; law prevents the emergence of repressive and authoritarian groups and individuals.
facts.quote: Judiciary helps to protect the rights of people. ... law prevents emergence of repressive and authoritarian groups and individuals.

facts.text: India is a Union of States; the Centre and the States have separate legislatures and executives, but there is one judicial system for the whole of India.
facts.quote: India is Union of States. The Centre and the Constituent States have a seperate legislature and executive. But there is one judicial system for the whole of India.

facts.text: There is no division of courts between the Centre and the States, so the judiciary in India is an integrated system.
facts.quote: There is no division of courts between the Centre and the Constituent States. This means that judiciary in India is an integrated system.

facts.text: The Supreme Court is the apex court; under it are the High Courts, which control the district courts, and lower courts are at the bottom.
facts.quote: The Supreme Court is the apex court under which there are High Courts. The High Courts control the district courts following which there are lower courts which are at the bottom of this structure.

facts.text: The Chief Justice of India (CJI) heads the Supreme Court of India.
facts.quote: The Chief Justice of India (CJI) heads the Supreme Court of India.

facts.text: The President appoints the Chief Justice of India and the other judges of the Supreme Court.
facts.quote: The President appoints the Chief Justice of India and other Judges of Supreme Court.

facts.text: By convention, the senior most judge of the Supreme Court is appointed as the Chief Justice.
facts.quote: By convention, the senior most judge of the Supreme Court is appointed as the Chief Justice.

facts.text: The independence of the judiciary is maintained so that judges can fearlessly carry out the function of giving justice.
facts.quote: The independence of the judiciary is maintained so as to enable the judges to fearlessly carry out the function of giving justice.

facts.text: The Constitution lays down the eligibility criteria for judges: a legal expert, one who has served as a High Court judge or an experienced advocate is considered eligible.
facts.quote: The Constitution lays down the eligibility criteria for the judges. A legal expert or one having served as the High Court judge or an experienced advocate is considered eligible.

facts.text: Judges are appointed by the President; this helps to avoid any political pressure.
facts.quote: Judges are appointed by the President. This helps to avoid any political pressure.

facts.text: Judges enjoy security of tenure; they cannot be removed for trivial reasons or for political motives.
facts.quote: Judges enjoy security of tenure. They cannot be removed from the post for trivial reasons or for political motives.

facts.text: The retirement age of Supreme Court judges is 65 years; for the High Court it is 62 years.
facts.quote: The retirement age of judges of the Supreme Court is 65 years, while for the High Court it is 62 years.

facts.text: The salaries of judges are drawn from the Consolidated Fund of India; no discussion takes place on this in the Parliament.
facts.quote: The salaries of judges are drawn from the Consolidated Fund of India, no discussion takes place on this issue in the Parliament.

facts.text: Personal criticisms cannot be made on judges for their acts and decisions; Contempt of Court is a punishable offense that protects judges and preserves the independence of the judiciary.
facts.quote: Personal criticisms cannot be made on judges for their acts and decisions. Contempt of Court is considered a punishable offense. This not only protects the judges from misguided/ wrongful criticism but also preserves the independence of the judiciary.

facts.text: The Parliament cannot discuss the decisions of the judges, but it can remove judges through the impeachment procedure.
facts.quote: The Parliament cannot discuss the decisions of the judges. However, it has the right to remove the judges from their position through the impeachment procedure.

facts.text: Judicial Activism: in the last few decades courts have become increasingly active and seek to fulfil the constitutional goals of justice and equality.
facts.quote: In the last few decades, this image of the court has undergone a change and they have become increasingly active. This means that the court now seeks to fulfill the constitutional goals of justice and equality.

facts.text: The court has tried to give legal protection to marginalised sections, women, tribal, workers, farmers and children; Public Interest Litigations have played an important role.
facts.quote: The court has tried to provide legal protection to the marginalised sections in society, women, tribal, workers, farmers, and children. Public Interest Litigations have played an important role in this regard.

facts.text: As a federal court, the Supreme Court settles disputes between the Union and the states, and between states.
facts.quote: As a federal court, it has the responsibility to settle disputes between the Union and the states; between the states and the Union and any state on one hand and one or more states on the other hand.

facts.text: The Supreme Court may give orders for the protection of the fundamental rights of citizens.
facts.quote: It may also give orders for protection of the fundamental rights of citizen.

facts.text: The Supreme Court reviews decrees and orders of lower courts and also reviews its own decisions.
facts.quote: To review decrees and orders of lower courts and also review its own decisions.

facts.text: When the President asks for advice on the legal aspects of matters of public importance, the Supreme Court provides the necessary advice.
facts.quote: In case the President asks for the advice of the Court to understand the legal aspects in matters of public importance, provide the necessary advice.

facts.text: The Supreme Court of India is in Delhi.
facts.quote: Supreme Court of India, Delhi

facts.text: Judicial Review: if a law of the Legislature or an act of the Executive violates the Constitution, the court declares it illegal and strikes it down; this protects the Constitution.
facts.quote: If any law passed by the Legislature or any act of the Executive violates any provision of the Constitution, the said law or act is declared illegal and struck down by the court. This power of the court is known as Judicial Review.

facts.text: Public Interest Litigation (PIL) refers to litigations filed on issues of public importance by individual citizens, social organisations or Non-Governmental Organisations on behalf of all people.
facts.quote: Public Interest Litigation (PIL) refers to litigations filed on issues of public importance by individual citizens, social organisations or Non-Governmental Organisations on behalf of the all people.

facts.text: The Court asked election candidates to declare their property and income details and educational qualifications through an affidavit, so voters vote on accurate information.
facts.quote: The Court had asked candidates contesting elections to declare their property and income details and educational qualifications through an affidavit. The aim was to ensure that the voters will vote on the basis of accurate information about the candidates.

facts.text: The Parliament has the power to establish a High Court in each Constituent State.
facts.quote: The Indian Union of states confers the Parliament with the power to establish a High Court in each Constituent State in the Union.

facts.text: Currently there are 24 High Courts in India.
facts.quote: Currently, there are 24 High Courts in India.

facts.text: A High Court has a Chief Justice along with other judges; all High Court judges are appointed by the President.
facts.quote: There is a Chief Justice along with other judges in the High Court. All judges of the High Court are appointed by the President.

facts.text: The Bombay High Court's jurisdiction covers Maharashtra and Goa, and the Union Territories of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.
facts.quote: The Bombay High Court's jurisdiction covers the states of Maharashtra and Goa, and the Union Territories of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.

facts.text: The High Court supervises and controls the lower courts in its jurisdiction and can give orders to protect fundamental rights.
facts.quote: To supervise and maintain control over the lower courts in its jurisdiction. Authority to give orders to protect fundamental rights.

facts.text: The Governor seeks the advice of the High Court while appointing judges in the district courts.
facts.quote: The Governor seeks the advice of the High Court while appointing judges in the district courts.

facts.text: District and lower courts are at the district and tehsil (taluka) level; people generally go to these courts; every District Court has one district judge.
facts.quote: These are courts at the district and tehsil (taluka) level. The people generally go to these courts. Every District Court has one district judge.

facts.text: There are two main branches of law: Civil law and Criminal law.
facts.quote: There are two main branches of law: (1) Civil law and (2) Criminal law.

facts.text: Civil law deals with conflicts that affect the rights of a person, for example land and property, rent agreement and divorce.
facts.quote: This law deals with conflicts which affect or interfere with the rights of a person. For example, Conflicts regarding land and property, rent agreement, divorce, etc.

facts.text: Serious crimes such as theft, robbery, dowry and murder come under criminal law; the first step is an FIR with the Police, then the police investigate and a petition is filed in court.
facts.quote: Serious crimes are dealt under criminal law. For example, theft, robbery, dowry, murder, etc. In these cases, the first step is to file a First Information Report (FIR) with the Police. The police investigates the matter and then a petition is filed in the court.

facts.text: If the charges are proved in a criminal case, there are provisions for severe punishment.
facts.quote: If the charges are proved, there are provisions for severe punishment.

facts.text: The judiciary in India has protected individual freedom, the federal system and the Constitution of India, and has strengthened democracy.
facts.quote: The judiciary in India has protected individual freedom, the federal system and the Constitution of India. Courts have played an important role in strengthening the democracy in India.
